test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 4 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Provincial autonomy was prescribed under Government of India Act of:
solution:
The correct answer is__** 1935.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India Act of **1935** is significant as it introduced the concept of provincial autonomy in British India.
 
• This act provided provinces with more legislative powers, allowing them to function with greater independence in certain areas.
 
• Provincial autonomy enabled provincial governments to legislate on a wider range of subjects, improving self-governance.
 
• The act aimed to address the growing demands for self-rule and respond to the Indian independence movement.
 
• **The 1935 Act** was the last major constitutional reform before India gained independence in 1947.
 
• Key Features of the 1935 Act:
 
 
• Established a federal structure with a division of powers between the Centre and provinces.
 
• Introduced a system of diarchy at the provincial level, allowing elected representatives to govern.
 
• Expanded the electorate and provided for separate electorates for different communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act, 1919**: This act introduced limited self-government but did not grant provincial autonomy as extensively as the 1935 act.
 
• **Government of India Act, 1937**: This act was enacted under the framework established by the 1935 act, but it was not the one that initially prescribed provincial autonomy.
 
• **Government of India Act, 1947**: This act marked the end of British rule in India and the partition of India and Pakistan, focusing more on independence than on administrative reforms.
 
• **Significance**: The act laid the groundwork for the eventual establishment of a democratic government in India, influencing the Indian Constitution adopted in 1950.
